request.description: Repose BOTH existing characters into ONE clear interaction key pose. Preserve the exact identities, native scale and pixel-art style of this input: LEFT Ataho, a broad-headed orange tiger with ivory muzzle, stocky short thick limbs, reddish-brown jacket, charcoal trousers, brown sash, wraps and ONE striped tail; RIGHT a gray-faced terracotta armoured soldier with the same helmet and brown segmented armour. His torso is distinctly BENT FORWARD about 60 degrees toward the right, broad head carried down/right, NEVER just a shallow crouch with a punching fist. BOTH of the tiger's bare feet remain visibly planted at the original y=128 baseline, one support foot braced. The ARMOURED SOLDIER is now DRAPED DIAGONALLY FACE-DOWN ACROSS the tiger's lower back/hip: his belly presses on the hip, head and chest on the RIGHT, bent knees and BOTH feet lifted on the LEFT. The soldier is a living articulated body with bent hips, shoulders and knees, NOT an upright or sideways rigid cutout. The tiger's near paw grips the soldier's sleeve/wrist forward/down on the right, the other forearm visibly WRAPS the soldier's waist. Make a firm continuous hand-to-sleeve and hip-to-belly contact. Soldier and tiger limbs remain distinct and attached to their correct bodies. The soldier is off balance and about to roll over the hip DOWN toward the right. Clear read: the tiger carries and turns the enemy, not punching, hugging chest to chest or holding a levitating soldier. No added characters, weapons, props, shadows, text, motion trails, impact effects, floor or camera change. Never merge their faces, hands, legs or costumes.
